methodhelp.clean_series: Sorts paired X/Y samples by increasing X and handles exactly equal X values. It does not interpolate or create a regular grid. Y values at duplicate X are averaged by default; first, last and error policies are also available. At least two finite samples and two distinct X values after cleanup are required. Use Sampling and gap inspection first if you want to inspect without changing the series.
methodhelp.affine: Y′ = scale × Y + offset; X is unchanged.
methodhelp.preprocess:
Sorts paired X/Y samples and handles duplicate X, then creates a grid and interpolates using the selected spacing. Defaults to the median cleaned adjacent interval and linear interpolation. No-resampling mode still sorts and deduplicates, but skips interpolation.
The grid starts at the smallest X without extrapolation. An endpoint off the grid is not appended. A denser grid adds estimates, not observations, and does not reconstruct missing sections. Split discontinuous records when necessary; this task does not automatically forbid interpolation across large gaps.
methodhelp.insolation_source: Top-of-atmosphere daily mean irradiance in W/m². Select solar longitude or a fixed non-leap month/day; dates are not year-specific historical Gregorian conversions.
methodhelp.seasonal_insolation: Seasonal mean irradiance, accumulated energy and duration. Date intervals exclude the end day. Fixed non-leap dates map to the prescribed year length; see seasonal conventions.
parameterhelp.fraction: Fraction of samples in a local LOWESS window, not a physical X-axis width.
parameterhelp.iterations: 0: ordinary LOWESS. Positive values enable robust reweighting; 5 is a common rLOWESS setting.
parameterhelp.nfft: 0 uses the input length. Zero padding refines the frequency grid but does not improve physical spectral resolution.
parameterhelp.fmax_ratio: Fraction of the Nyquist frequency to publish. Background fitting and peak detection still use the full spectrum.
parameterhelp.peak_prominence: Absolute prominence in PSD units. 0 disables the absolute threshold; the relative threshold can still apply. Peak detection does not establish statistical significance.
parameterhelp.peak_distance: Minimum index distance between retained peaks. Stronger prominence wins, then height.
parameterhelp.peak_width: Width at half prominence, measured in frequency bins. Zero disables this filter.
parameterhelp.peak_height: Minimum PSD at the peak, independent of the significance curves. Zero retains all nonnegative candidates.
parameterhelp.peak_radius: 0 searches the full spectrum. A positive radius limits baseline search to that many bins on each side, changing prominence and width.
parameterhelp.interpolation: Linear is the default. Cubic is a natural cubic spline; Akima is a local piecewise cubic method. No method is silently forced.
parameterhelp.duplicate_policy: Duplicate means exactly equal X, not repeated Y. Average combines Y; first/last refer to original input order.
parameterhelp.skip_invalid_rows: By default a missing or invalid X or Y reports the source line. Enable this option to skip and count these rows. Empty fields, NaN, NA, N/A and NULL denote missing values, ignoring case. Completely blank lines are always ignored.
parameterhelp.age_start_ka: Age before J2000, positive into the past; not BP relative to 1950.
parameterhelp.age_end_ka: Older end of the interval, at most 50000 ka before J2000.
parameterhelp.age_step_ka: La2004 native spacing is 1 ka. Finer spacing interpolates; seasonal integration allows at most 20000 ages.
parameterhelp.latitude_deg: North is positive, south negative; both poles ±90° are supported.
parameterhelp.solar_longitude_deg: 0° vernal equinox, 90° June solstice, 180° autumnal equinox, 270° December solstice.
parameterhelp.solar_constant: Radiation at 1 AU. Default 1365 W/m² is explicit and adjustable.
parameterhelp.season_basis: Choose solar longitude or Gregorian month lengths without leap days. The 365 calendar slots span 365.24219876 24-hour days; equinox is fixed at March 21 noon. This is not a historical Gregorian reconstruction.
parameterhelp.month_start: Month 1–12; February has 28 days in the declared fixed calendar.
parameterhelp.day_start: Daily task evaluates the chosen date at noon. Seasonal task starts at midnight.
parameterhelp.day_end: Midnight at the end date, excluded. June 1 to September 1 includes June–August. Same dates mean a full year; earlier end dates wrap forward.
parameterhelp.season_start_deg: Forward integration in solar longitude with Kepler time weighting, not an unweighted longitude average.
parameterhelp.season_end_deg: End <= start wraps forward; equal bounds mean a complete year.

methodhelp.gaussian_filter: Uniform sampling required. Removes the mean; band edges are half-power points. Gaussian zero-pads before filtering.
methodhelp.taner_filter: Uniform sampling required. Removes the mean; uses an N-point periodic filter and a separate amplitude envelope.
methodhelp.hilbert_envelope: Envelope of the selected parent output; no filtering is inserted. Narrow-band signals give the clearest amplitude interpretation.

parameterhelp.upper_frequency: The amplitude gain is 1/sqrt(2) at both band edges; the corresponding power gain is 1/2.
parameterhelp.rolloff_exponent: Controls the Taner filter band-edge decay parameter c=10^q, with q=12 by default; this is not dB per octave.

methodhelp.evolution_fft:
One-sided PSD in complete moving windows, showing how cycle structure varies with time/depth. X must be strictly increasing and regularly spaced; explicitly clean/resample first if needed. Map columns are window centers and rows are frequencies. The mean of window spectra is not the full-record spectrum.
Choose window length for the cycles of interest, then choose step samples, overlap or target window count. New tasks default to 20% span, target 500 windows, 4× FFT, linear detrending, rectangular taper, per-window normalization and square-root power display. All remain editable; this is not a universal optimum. Successful previews show resolved window samples, step, overlap and FFT samples.
Greater overlap densifies window positions; FFT padding densifies frequencies. Neither improves true frequency resolution. Per-window normalization removes absolute strength differences. Amplitude colors and interpolation do not change stored power. Only complete windows are used, without whole-series end padding or significance testing. See the user guide for preset attribution and cross-software comparison limits.
Automatic modes resolve independently from each actual upstream input, whether or not its editor was opened. Batch actions copy rules. Restore default parameters affects the current input; use the batch action afterwards to reset other inputs.
methodhelp.evolution_mtm:
Adaptive MTM spectra in complete moving windows, showing cycle structure across time/depth. X must be strictly increasing and regularly spaced; there is no implicit resampling. Choose a window containing enough cycles, then a sample step, overlap or target window count. The latter resolves an integer step from this node's actual input; the number of windows does not exceed the target.
NW controls the smoothing/resolution tradeoff in spectral estimation. Target count controls window-position density, a different choice. Successful previews show resolved window samples, step, overlap and FFT samples. Per-window normalization is off by default; enabling it removes absolute power differences between windows. The arithmetic mean of window spectra is not full-record MTM. No pointwise or whole-map significance test is provided, and no boundary padding is added.
methodhelp.select_interval: Keeps or removes X/Y samples in a closed interval, preserving row order. No interpolation or gap closure.
methodhelp.demean: Subtracts the arithmetic mean from Y; X and units are unchanged.
methodhelp.standardize: Subtracts the mean from Y and divides by the selected standard deviation to obtain a dimensionless series. Not defined for constant series.
methodhelp.sampling_check:
Inspects X order, duplicate coordinates, regularity and large intervals without changing the input series. Read the summary first, then the interval and gap details. Flags identify locations to inspect and do not establish a sedimentary hiatus.
Statistics cover the full input. Each detail table retains at most the first 4096 rows in input order; inspection is not restricted to 4096 samples. Truncation is recorded in the calculation report, and export cannot restore unretained details. Preview display budgets are a separate limit.
parameterhelp.evo_window: Enter samples. With spacing dx and length L, the endpoint span is (L-1)*dx and the Fourier duration is L*dx. For example, 100 samples at spacing 0.2 give a Fourier duration of 20. Require at least 8 samples and no more than the input length. Choose the window for the periods of interest.
parameterhelp.evo_step: Step S in samples; the physical step is S*spacing. The number of complete windows is floor((N-L)/S)+1. For 705 samples and a 128-sample window, step 16 gives 37 windows; step 1 gives 578. Only complete windows are used; unused tail samples are reported. Smaller steps increase computation.
parameterhelp.evo_nfft: 0 uses the window length; an explicit value must be at least that length. Frequency spacing is 1/(FFT length*sample spacing). For spacing 0.2 and FFT length 400 it is 0.0125. Zero padding densifies the grid, without improving the window's physical frequency resolution.
parameterhelp.evo_trend: Each window removes its mean or fitted linear trend before spectral estimation.
parameterhelp.evo_frequency_ratio: Retained for legacy workflows. The output limit is ratio/(2*sample spacing). New workflows use Maximum frequency; explicitly editing that field, including confirming 0 for automatic, clears the legacy ratio. MTM weights and window-normalization maxima use the full frequency range.
parameterhelp.evo_nw: NW controls MTM spectral smoothing/resolution within each window, not the count of moving positions. Require NW=1 or 1.25–32, with NW<window samples/2. NW=1 uses 2 DPSS tapers; otherwise round(2×NW)−1. Larger NW generally smooths more and may merge nearby peaks.
parameterhelp.evo_taper: Periodic Hann or rectangular taper, normalized by its squared-energy sum for PSD units.
parameterhelp.interval_lower: Uses the current X-axis unit; the lower bound is included.
parameterhelp.interval_upper: Uses the current X-axis unit; the upper bound is included and must not be below the lower bound.
parameterhelp.gap_factor: Flags positive adjacent intervals greater than this multiple of their median. A flag does not by itself prove a sedimentary hiatus.
warning.evolution_descriptive: No significance test is provided. The mean spectrum averages windows, not the full-record estimate. With window normalization enabled, both outputs contain dimensionless relative power.
warning.evolution_unconverged: Some MTM windows reached the adaptive iteration limit; see the report count.
warning.selection_gap: Removing samples may create gaps; downstream methods still check their own sampling requirements.
warning.sampling_unordered: X is not strictly increasing; the original data is retained unchanged.
warning.sampling_nonuniform: X is not uniformly spaced at relative tolerance 1e−6. No resampling was performed.
warning.sampling_gap: Large positive sampling intervals were found. These are data-quality flags, not a hiatus interpretation.
diagnostic.EVOLUTION_BUDGET.summary: Evolutionary spectrum exceeds the work or memory budget.
diagnostic.EVOLUTION_BUDGET.suggestion: Reduce the target window count or increase the step, reduce window/FFT length, or select a shorter input interval. Limits: one million input samples, 20000 windows, two million output cells.
diagnostic.EVOLUTION_PARAMETERS.suggesti: The window must contain at least 8 samples and fit the current node input. Increase the span percentage if it resolves to fewer samples. Check 1 ≤ step ≤ window, FFT length ≥ window, NW and the frequency limit.
diagnostic.EVOLUTION_FAILED.summary: Evolutionary spectrum could not be computed.
diagnostic.EVOLUTION_FAILED.suggestion: Inspect the numerical details and input scale. The task did not produce a valid result.
diagnostic.SERIES_BUDGET.summary: Series exceeds the one-million-sample task limit.
diagnostic.SERIES_BUDGET.suggestion: Select a shorter input interval before running this task.
diagnostic.STANDARDIZE_CONSTANT.summary: A constant series cannot be standardized.
diagnostic.STANDARDIZE_CONSTANT.suggesti: Its standard deviation is zero; use demean if a zero series is intended.
diagnostic.SELECTION_INTERVAL.summary: The lower X bound must not exceed the upper bound.
diagnostic.SELECTION_INTERVAL.suggestion: Enter finite bounds in the current X-axis unit.
diagnostic.SELECTION_EMPTY.summary: No samples remain after interval selection.
diagnostic.SELECTION_EMPTY.suggestion: Check the bounds, X units, and whether keep or remove is selected.
parameterhelp.smooth_window: Odd, at most 501 and no larger than the input. A point-count window. Moving mean clips edges; SG fits the first/last full window at the edges.
parameterhelp.smooth_degree: 0–5 and smaller than the window. Requires uniform sampling; default degree 2. Smoothing only, without differentiation.
parameterhelp.psd_window: At least 8 samples and no larger than the input. Complete segments only; no automatic shortening or edge padding.
parameterhelp.psd_overlap: Must be smaller than the segment length. Default 128 of 256 samples (50%); check this value after changing the segment length.
parameterhelp.psd_nfft: 0 uses record/segment length. Explicit values cannot be shorter; maximum 262144. Zero padding densifies the grid, not the physical resolution.
parameterhelp.psd_taper: One-sided physical PSD normalized by the sum of squared window weights; periodic Hann by default.
parameterhelp.psd_trend: FFT detrends the full record; Welch detrends each segment before estimating its spectrum.
warning.smoothing_changes_signal: Smoothing alters amplitudes and frequency content; it is not a significance test or confidence interval.
warning.smoothing_point_window: Nonuniform sampling: the moving average uses neighboring points; its physical X span varies.
warning.psd_descriptive: Physical PSD without significance thresholds or a peak index. Use MTM for the existing detected-frequency search.
diagnostic.SIGNAL_BUDGET.summary: The sample, window or work budget was exceeded.
diagnostic.SIGNAL_BUDGET.suggestion: Smoothing: at most 501 window points, one million samples and 100 million products. Spectra: FFT at most 262144, segments at most 20000. Select a shorter interval or reduce the window/FFT size.
diagnostic.SIGNAL_PARAMETERS.summary: The smoothing or spectral parameters are incompatible.
diagnostic.SIGNAL_PARAMETERS.suggestion: Check odd smoothing window and degree < window; spectral segments >= 8 and <= input, overlap < segment, and FFT length >= record/segment.
diagnostic.SIGNAL_FAILED.suggestion: Inspect diagnostic details and the input magnitude; no valid output was produced.

parameterhelp.ls_min_frequency: In inverse X units. 0 uses 1/record span. Uses the actual uneven X coordinates, without interpolation or sorting; at least 5 samples.
parameterhelp.ls_max_frequency: 0 uses 0.5/median adjacent spacing. This is a search heuristic, not a strict Nyquist limit for uneven sampling. A custom upper limit may be larger or smaller.
parameterhelp.ls_samples_per_peak: Spacing is 1/(record span × density), default 5. A denser search does not increase physical resolution. At most 65536 frequencies and 50 million sample-frequency pairs. Output is normalized fit power (0–1), not PSD or significance probability.
parameterhelp.butter_cutoff: In inverse X units; uniform sampling required. Cutoff/Nyquist must be 0.0001–0.9999. Gain is 1/sqrt(2) at the single-pass cutoff and 0.5 after both passes. The response curve shows the combined amplitude gain.
parameterhelp.butter_order: 1–10, default 4; two passes double the effective order. Each end uses 3×(order+1) points of odd reflection; input must be longer. Low-pass preserves a constant baseline, not necessarily the exact sample mean of every finite record.
warning.lomb_normalization: Equal-weight floating-mean fit; power is the fractional residual reduction relative to a constant model. It is not PSD, confidence or false-alarm probability.
warning.lomb_auto_frequency: Automatic upper frequency is 0.5/median spacing: a search convention, not a strict Nyquist limit for uneven data. Check the band against your scientific target.
warning.lomb_rank: Some frequencies have rank-deficient harmonic columns. Fits use the identifiable subspace; completely degenerate bins are zero. Counts are recorded in the report.
warning.butterworth_boundary: Forward-backward filtering uses odd reflection and steady initial states. Edge effects remain, especially when the cutoff period approaches the record length.
warning.butterworth_cutoff: Cutoff is defined for one pass; combined amplitude gain at cutoff is 0.5 (about −6 dB). Inspect the amplitude-response output.
diagnostic.SPECTRAL_EXTENSION_BUDGET.sum: Input or frequency grid exceeds the computation budget.
diagnostic.SPECTRAL_EXTENSION_BUDGET.sug: For Lomb–Scargle, narrow the frequency interval or lower grid density: at most 65536 frequencies and 50 million sample-frequency pairs. Filtering allows one million samples. Data are not silently reduced.
diagnostic.SPECTRAL_EXTENSION_PARAMETERS: Frequency, record length or filter order is incompatible with the data.
Check the details and parameter help. Lomb–Scargle needs a positive nonempty frequency band; Butterworth requires more than 3×(order+1) samples.
diagnostic.SPECTRAL_EXTENSION_FAILED.sum: Spectral estimation or filtering could not complete.
diagnostic.SPECTRAL_EXTENSION_FAILED.sug: Inspect the diagnostic details and check data, frequency range and parameters.
diagnostic.LOMB_NO_VARIANCE.summary: The data have no usable variance for normalized Lomb–Scargle.
diagnostic.LOMB_NO_VARIANCE.suggestion: A constant series has no identifiable periodic variation. Choose varying data or check column selection and upstream operations.
diagnostic.BUTTERWORTH_CUTOFF.summary: Butterworth cutoff is unsuitable for this sampling interval; Nyquist is {nyquist}.
diagnostic.BUTTERWORTH_CUTOFF.suggestion: Use inverse X units. Cutoff/Nyquist must be within 0.0001–0.9999. Sampling intervals are not changed automatically.
parameterhelp.chrono_depth_unit: Actual unit of input X, default m. Must match nonempty input metadata; otherwise this explicit declaration is used with a warning.
parameterhelp.chrono_age_unit: Default ka (1000 years). Used for the first age and output; for Apply age model it is also the unit of the control-table age column, not inferred from its header.
parameterhelp.chrono_age_reference: Records the reference only; no epoch shift is applied. BP1950 and J2000 use their named epochs; relative is user-defined. Age increases with depth. Unspecified is not assumed to be before present.
parameterhelp.chrono_rate_unit: Y must be a positive sedimentation rate, default cm/ka. Existing metadata must match; kyr/ka and Myr/Ma aliases are accepted. Zero/negative rates cannot encode hiatuses or erosion here.
parameterhelp.chrono_first_age: Assigned to the FIRST input depth, default 0 in the selected age unit; not automatically tied to depth zero.
parameterhelp.chrono_rate_rule: Default left-constant: each interval uses its left-end sedimentation rate to calculate the age increment; the final rate is validated but unused. Linear-rate mode integrates the reciprocal of a linearly varying rate, not the reciprocal of a mean rate.
parameterhelp.chrono_model_file: Choose a depth–age table with at least two rows, including CSV exported by Sedimentation rate to age model. Default columns 1 and 2; max 4 MiB/100000 controls. Both columns must increase strictly; no automatic cleanup.
parameterhelp.chrono_model_depth_unit: Unit of the control-table depth column, converted to the input depth unit. The age column uses the Age unit setting.
parameterhelp.chrono_delimiter: Uses the normal import parser: automatic, comma, tab or whitespace. Blank lines and # comments are ignored.
parameterhelp.chrono_header: Auto detection examines the selected columns. Yes consumes the first row; No parses it as data. Invalid numeric rows fail rather than being skipped.
parameterhelp.chrono_depth_column: One-based control-table depth column; must differ from the age column.
parameterhelp.chrono_age_column: One-based control-table age column. Uncertainty columns are not interpreted as confidence intervals.
parameterhelp.chrono_boundary: Default rejects uncovered data without deleting rows. Explicit linear extrapolation extends endpoint secants and reports the count. No automatic resampling follows.
warning.chronology_deterministic: Deterministic age conversion: no age uncertainty estimate or geological validation of the controls.
warning.chronology_left_rate: Each interval uses its left rate; the final rate is validated as positive but not integrated.
warning.chronology_declared_units: Input units are missing; the explicitly selected task units were used. Check their physical meaning.
warning.chronology_no_resampling: Only X is converted; Y and sample count are unchanged. Resulting ages may be irregular; resample explicitly if a later method requires it.
warning.chronology_control_snapshot: The controls and file hash used are retained. Later executions reread that path; use preview Recalculate after external edits.
warning.chronology_extrapolated: Linear extrapolation was used; see the report for its sample count. Extrapolation adds no age constraints.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_UNIT.summary: Input units conflict with task settings.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_UNIT.suggestion: Check import and task units; do not mistake time for depth or an arbitrary signal for sedimentation rate.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_SHAPE.summary: Age conversion requires at least two valid pairs.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_SHAPE.suggestion: Check input length, controls and parameters.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_DEPTH_ORDER.summar: Depth must strictly increase without duplicates.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_DEPTH_ORDER.sugges: Inspect the point number; explicitly clean/sort data if appropriate. This task never edits rows automatically.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_AGE_ORDER.summary: Control ages must strictly increase with depth.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_AGE_ORDER.suggesti: Check reversals, repeated ages, selected columns and age direction; hiatuses/erosion need a separate model.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_RATE_POSITIVE.summ: Every sedimentation rate must be finite and positive.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_RATE_POSITIVE.sugg: Includes the final row; check units, zeros, negatives and invalid values.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_COVERAGE.summary: Input depth lies outside age-control coverage.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_COVERAGE.suggestio: Check depth units, extend controls, select a covered interval or explicitly enable linear extrapolation.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_NUMERIC.summary: Age/rate exceeds numeric range or loses resolvable strict ordering.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_NUMERIC.suggestion: Check units, extreme rates, very large age offsets and tiny intervals; Inf/NaN or flattened ages are not returned.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_BUDGET.summary: Age conversion exceeds current resource limits.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_BUDGET.suggestion: At most one million input points; control tables at most 4 MiB/100000 rows. Select the needed range first.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_PARAMETERS.suggest: Inspect details, units and parameter help.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_MODEL_FILE.suggest: Choose a control table in step settings; a model CSV exported by the rate task is supported.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_COLUMNS.summary: Depth and age columns must differ.
diagnostic.CHRONOLOGY_COLUMNS.suggestion: Select different numeric columns using one-based column numbers.
parameterhelp.target_age_ma: 0–4000 million years before present; default 300 Ma. Waltham (2015) envelope model, not an orbital phase solution.
parameterhelp.target_component: Obliquity and four climatic-precession components vary with age. Five eccentricity frequency envelopes are fixed approximations from Table 1.
parameterhelp.cycle_period_source: Manual by default. Model midpoint uses the selected Waltham envelope midpoint, converted from ka to the Age unit. It is not a measured period.
parameterhelp.cycle_period: Default 41 in Age unit (default ka). One full cycle between consecutive selected peaks OR troughs, never alternating peaks and troughs.
parameterhelp.cycle_extremum: Choose peaks or troughs of a suitable signal; filter explicitly beforehand if needed. Flat tops/bottoms count once, at the central sample (left of two central samples). Endpoints are excluded.
parameterhelp.cycle_min_relief: Default 0 in Y units. Peak height above the higher adjacent inter-peak valley; troughs use the inverted signal. This is not global peak prominence.
parameterhelp.cycle_min_distance: Default 0 in Input depth unit. Retain stronger local relief first; ties prefer earlier markers. Equality is allowed. Suppression changes cycle counts and cannot detect missing cycles.
parameterhelp.cycle_first_age_mode: By default, the first marker is assigned an age of one full period. Choose a specified age to enter an absolute or relative age when a dated marker is available.
parameterhelp.cycle_first_age: Age of the FIRST selected marker, in Age unit. It is not the first input row. Ages increase with depth.
parameterhelp.cycle_extend_ends: Off by default: model contains selected markers only. When enabled, extend the first/last age-depth secants to the input ends; this adds no independent age constraint.
warning.target_envelope: These are model envelopes, not calibrated 95% confidence intervals, orbital phases or a statistical detection of astronomical forcing.
warning.target_eccentricity: Eccentricity periods use fixed Table 1 frequency envelopes; geological age does not change these approximations.
warning.cycle_count_assumption: Each consecutive selected marker is assigned one full cycle. Missing or double cycles are not inferred. Tuning imposes periodicity and is not independent evidence for astronomical forcing.
warning.cycle_model_midpoint: Only the target midpoint sets the duration. Its model envelope is recorded, but not propagated as an age uncertainty.
diagnostic.TARGET_PERIOD.summary: Cannot evaluate the astronomical period model.
diagnostic.TARGET_PERIOD.suggestion: Use a finite age in 0–4000 Ma and a supported component; inspect the detailed numeric message.
diagnostic.CYCLE_ANCHORS.summary: Fewer than two usable same-phase cycle markers.
diagnostic.CYCLE_ANCHORS.suggestion: Use at least three paired samples with at least two interior peaks or troughs; inspect thresholds, input range and any prior filtering. Constant data cannot define cycles.
parameterhelp.coco_target: Manual periods by default. Optional Waltham midpoints select E405, E124, E95, obliquity, P1, P2 and P4; this does not load a La2004 time series.
parameterhelp.coco_periods: Enter 2–16 positive periods separated by commas or spaces. Defaults 405,125,95,41,24,22,19 ka are a modern example; use age-appropriate periods for older records. All frequencies must be below the band limit.
parameterhelp.coco_powers: Positive powers, one per period, not amplitudes. Defaults 1,1,1,0.64,0.36,0.36,0.36 correspond to amplitudes 1,1,1,0.8,0.6,0.6,0.6. No adaptive fitting.
parameterhelp.coco_rate_min: Positive sedimentation rate. X must be increasing, uniformly sampled depth; no automatic sorting or resampling.
parameterhelp.coco_rate_max: Upper bound; rates are minimum plus integer multiples of the step. No off-grid endpoint is appended.
parameterhelp.coco_rate_step: At most 2000 rates. The full band and every target must be resolved; excluded candidates remain in the diagnostic table.
parameterhelp.coco_max_frequency: Default 0.06. Compare non-DC bins up to this limit; short ancient precession periods may require a higher limit. The full band must lie within candidate Nyquist.
parameterhelp.coco_padding: 1–4; FFT length is the next power of two at least factor times N. Padding refines the grid, not physical resolution.
parameterhelp.coco_detrend: Default removes only the mean; none or linear detrending is optional. Apply the same rule to data and target bases. No red-noise removal or implicit LOWESS.
warning.coco_descriptive: Descriptive spectral matching only: no significance test or rate confidence interval. High correlation does not prove astronomical forcing. The best candidate is not a confirmed rate; no age model is created.
warning.coco_target: The fixed-weight target averages sine and cosine powers to avoid arbitrary phase interference. It uses neither adaptive weights nor red-noise background subtraction. Nearby targets may remain unresolved; this count is not a detection count.
warning.coco_exclusions: Some rates were excluded. Status: 0 eligible, 1 band above Nyquist, 2 insufficient resolution/bins, 3 constant spectrum. Correlations are valid only where eligible=1; other zeros are placeholders.
progress.coco_scan: Scanning rates and comparing target spectra
diagnostic.COCO_BUDGET.suggestion: See details for the specific limit. Input size, FFT length, rate grid and cache have separate limits; adjust sampling, the rate grid or padding for the exceeded limit.
diagnostic.COCO_NO_SCORE.suggestion: Check whether the series is constant and whether its sampling and length cover the full target band. See details; resampling or target changes require explicit settings.
diagnostic.COCO_PARAMETERS.summary: Invalid COCO parameters or numeric range.
diagnostic.COCO_PARAMETERS.suggestion: Check periods/powers, units, scan range, simulation count/test level, window length and step. See the specific cause in details.
parameterhelp.coco_null: Default: fixed-parameter Gaussian AR(1); rho=0 is white noise. Random spectral peaks are a literature reference model, not a general time-series false-positive guarantee.
parameterhelp.coco_rho: Specify independently of the tested data. Fitting rho to this series does not give an exact test. Default 0; |rho|<1. Replay detrending, FFT and rate scanning on stationary Gaussian AR(1) draws; upstream processing is not replayed.
parameterhelp.coco_null_peaks: 0: count strict local periodogram peaks, excluding zero and Nyquist frequencies; otherwise use the specified count. Simulated peaks have random positions and heights, with width 2 Rayleigh frequency-resolution units. No red-noise background subtraction.
parameterhelp.coco_simulations: Default 199; minimum p resolution is 1/(B+1). Increase B for final analyses when budget permits; predeclare the target, band and rate grid.
parameterhelp.coco_seed: A fixed seed reproduces the same input and parameters; tasks do not share mutable RNG state. Do not select a seed by its result.
parameterhelp.coco_alpha: Default 0.05; must be at least 1/(B+1). Decide using p<=alpha; the critical value is a plotting aid. After selecting a best rate, use the scan-adjusted or global-scan p value.
parameterhelp.ecoco_window: Full windows only, at least two. Each window must resolve the specified target; adjust the window or target if too short. No automatic resampling.
parameterhelp.ecoco_step: 1 to the window length. At most 512 full windows; an incomplete trailing window is omitted and reported, never padded.
warning.coco_fixed_null: Tests the current input against stationary Gaussian AR(1) with independently specified rho; rho=0 is white noise. No rho fitting or replay of upstream filters. Calibration requires the declared null; detrending=none also requires zero mean.
warning.coco_random_reference: Random-peak p values compare with a reference spectrum of 2-Rayleigh half-sine peaks at random positions/heights, not arbitrary red-noise data. Automatic peak count comes from the observed spectrum; no red-noise background removal.
warning.coco_scan_test: Pointwise p is for a predeclared individual rate. Scan-adjusted/global p uses each replicate’s maximum positive correlation over this fixed grid; it does not cover parameter searches, multiple files or a sliding map. Significance does not prove astronomical causation or give a rate confidence interval.
warning.ecoco_descriptive: The eCOCO map is descriptive local spectral matching, with no pointwise or whole-map significance. Best candidates are selected independently per window and may jump; no age model is generated or smoothed.
warning.ecoco_tail: An incomplete trailing window was omitted; see unused_tail_samples in the report. No edge-window padding or extrapolation.

parameterhelp.peak_relative_prominence: Default 0.1% of the full spectrum power range. Suppresses tiny tail oscillations; lowering it preserves weaker peaks. 0 disables this amplitude filter. Not a statistical significance test. Absolute and relative thresholds both apply; roundoff-sized fluctuations are excluded.

parameterhelp.frequency_max: In inverse input-axis units (e.g. 1/ka). Crops the spectrum, thresholds and peak table, affecting saved and downstream data; fitting and peak detection use the full spectrum. 0 selects automatic; values above Nyquist are capped. See the guide for legacy ratios.
parameterhelp.factor: Y′ = scale factor × Y + offset. A negative factor reverses the sign of Y; X is unchanged.
parameterhelp.offset: Constant added to Y after scaling, in the same units as Y. X is unchanged.
parameterhelp.ar1_precision: Each reference model uses 999 screening simulations. Standard mode uses the first 199 for analysis statistics; fine uses 999. These are not totals for the task; fine mode costs more and may exceed budgets.
parameterhelp.ar1_seed: Controls the reference simulations. Fix the seed for reproducibility rather than selecting it to obtain significance.
parameterhelp.ar1_lowess: Applies the same internal LOWESS to the observation and each reference simulation. Upstream workflow steps are not replayed.
parameterhelp.ar1_fraction: Fraction of samples in each internal LOWESS neighborhood. Used only when internal LOWESS is enabled; robust iterations are fixed at zero.
parameterhelp.ar1_cache: Reuses reference simulations with matching settings. Disabling this regenerates them without changing the test definition.
parameterhelp.method: Default variance-normalized, scale-corrected mode divides power by the input sample variance and wavelet scale. Raw-power mode displays squared wavelet-coefficient magnitude. Scale ranges and AR(1) background estimates also differ. Switching modes recalculates the result.
parameterhelp.mother: Morlet, Paul or DOG mother wavelet. Scale-to-period conversion and cone-of-influence conventions depend on the mother.
parameterhelp.parameter: Morlet requires a frequency parameter of at least 5; Paul requires an integer order; DOG requires an even integer order.
parameterhelp.dj: Spacing between scales in log2 units. Smaller values refine the scale grid at greater computational and memory cost, without increasing the resolution of the input.
parameterhelp.significance: Computes the nominal local 95% AR1 threshold and power ratio. A ratio above 1 exceeds the local threshold; it is not a global test of the time-frequency map.
parameterhelp.retain_mean: After subtracting the fitted trend, add the mean of that trend to preserve the input mean. This is not simply adding the input mean. The trend output is unchanged.
parameterhelp.etp_e: Weight of the standardized eccentricity component; zero excludes it.
parameterhelp.etp_t: Weight of the standardized obliquity component; zero excludes it.
parameterhelp.etp_p: Weight of standardized climatic precession; the default is −1. Changing its sign reverses the component.
parameterhelp.delimiter: Selects the column delimiter or automatic detection. File-reading options are configured per file in the input panel.
parameterhelp.header: A header row is not read as numeric data. Automatic detection examines the selected columns.
parameterhelp.x_column: Selects the X column for age, depth or another independent coordinate. Displayed column numbers start at 1.
parameterhelp.y_column: Selects the measured Y values. This must differ from the X column; displayed column numbers start at 1.
parameterhelp.latitude_end_deg: Northern bound of the latitude grid; north is positive and south is negative. Must exceed the southern bound.
parameterhelp.nw: Time–half-bandwidth product. Must equal 1 or be at least 1.25, and remain below half the sample count. Increasing it usually reduces variance and broadens peaks.
parameterhelp.ar1: Fits an AR1 background and produces nominal pointwise thresholds. This is distinct from the separate AR1 global test.
parameterhelp.swa: Produces SWA backgrounds, nominal thresholds and FDR curves. With fitted backgrounds, actual false discovery rates are not guaranteed to match nominal levels.
parameterhelp.logfit: Fits the AR1 background in log-power space. Does not change the displayed axis scale of the power spectrum.
parameterhelp.mc_simulations: Number of simulations for the archived experimental test. More simulations refine Monte Carlo probabilities but take longer.
parameterhelp.mc_alpha: Nominal significance level for the archived experimental test. Approximate calibration with an estimated correlation coefficient does not guarantee this level.
parameterhelp.mc_seed: A fixed seed and identical parameters reproduce the simulation settings.
parameterhelp.mc_estimate_rho: Estimates the AR1 coefficient from the input. This is an approximate parametric bootstrap, not a known-background test.
parameterhelp.mc_fixed_rho: Used when estimation is disabled. Specify it in advance from independent information, rather than treating an estimate from the current data as known.
parameterhelp.spacing_mode: Keeps the cleaned sampling positions, or creates a regular grid from the mean, median, minimum, maximum or specified spacing of cleaned X values.
parameterhelp.spacing: Specified sampling interval in X units. Used only in fixed-spacing mode.
parameterhelp.month_end: Ending month, from 1 to 12, in the fixed no-leap calendar. The end date is excluded from the integration interval.
parameterhelp.interval_action: Keeps or removes samples within the interval. Both endpoints are included.
parameterhelp.count: Number of generated samples. X starts at zero and ends at (sample count − 1) × sampling interval.
parameterhelp.step: X spacing between adjacent samples, in the same units as the period.
parameterhelp.period: Period of the sinusoid in X units. Frequency is the reciprocal of the period.
parameterhelp.amplitude: Amplitude of the sinusoidal component about its centerline. Peak-to-peak amplitude is twice its absolute value.
parameterhelp.slope: Linear trend increment per X unit. Zero adds no linear trend.
parameterhelp.standardize_sd: Subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation: N−1 for sample SD, N for population SD. Constant series cannot be standardized.
parameterhelp.mtm.smooth_window: Smoothing window as a fraction of spectral bins, from 0.05 to 0.25. This is not a sample count and does not modify the input series.
parameterhelp.mtm_ar1_simulation.nw: The archived experimental task uses an integer NW below half the sample count.
methodhelp.apply_age_model: Assigns ages by interpolation in a depth–age control table, with explicit boundary behavior.
methodhelp.butterworth_highpass: Forward–backward Butterworth high-pass filtering of regularly sampled data.
methodhelp.butterworth_lowpass: Forward–backward Butterworth low-pass filtering of regularly sampled data.
methodhelp.coco_monte_carlo: Evaluates a fixed-target COCO scan with simulated series; results depend on the targets, rate range and noise model.
methodhelp.coco_scan: Scans candidate sedimentation rates against fixed target periods. A scan optimum alone does not validate an age model.
methodhelp.cwt: Continuous wavelet time-frequency analysis of regularly sampled data, with power, cone of influence and applicable local significance outputs.
methodhelp.cycle_age_model: Assigns ages cycle by cycle from selected peaks or troughs; depends on extremum selection, missing cycles and interval selection.
methodhelp.database_grid: Reads a saved grid output for use in a workflow.
methodhelp.database_series: Reads a saved data series for use in a workflow.
methodhelp.database_spectrum: Reads a saved spectrum output for use in a workflow.
methodhelp.database_table: Reads a saved numerical table for use in a workflow.
methodhelp.detrend_lowess: Estimates a local LOWESS trend and outputs detrended data and the trend separately. The window is a fraction of samples.
methodhelp.etp_source: Weighted combination of standardized eccentricity, obliquity and climatic precession from La2004.
methodhelp.evolution_coco: Runs fixed-target COCO scans in moving windows to display candidate sedimentation rates along the record.
methodhelp.fft_spectrum: Estimates one-sided PSD from the full input. X must be strictly increasing and uniform, with at least 8 samples; no automatic resampling. Choose the input interval, detrending and taper before padding. FFT length 0 uses the full input; explicit length cannot be shorter. PSD peak height is not signal amplitude. No significance thresholds are supplied.
methodhelp.input_series: Supplies a bound data series to the workflow.
methodhelp.linear_detrend: Fits and subtracts the least-squares line of Y against X, with separate residual and trend outputs.
methodhelp.lomb_scargle: Analyzes irregular sampling directly. Floating-mean fitted power is normalized to 0–1; it is not PSD or a significance probability.
methodhelp.milankovitch_period: Returns orbital-period targets and model ranges at a specified geological age, not an orbital phase solution.
methodhelp.moving_average: Smooths a series with a centered window measured in samples, shortened at the ends.
methodhelp.mtm: Multitaper power spectra require regular sampling. AR1 95% and SWA 95% are approximate pointwise thresholds, not global spectrum tests. FDR q=0.05 uses a bandwidth dependence correction; actual FDR control has not been established for fitted backgrounds. Peak outcomes: 1 passed, 0 not passed, -1 not evaluated or unavailable. Local peaks alone do not establish significant cycles.
methodhelp.mtm_ar1_simulation: Archived experimental test, hidden from the task catalogue. Approximate bootstrap with an estimated correlation coefficient does not replace the AR1 global test.
methodhelp.orbital_source: La2004 eccentricity, obliquity and climatic precession, with ages referenced to J2000.
methodhelp.savitzky_golay: Local polynomial smoothing of regularly sampled data. The window must be odd and exceed the polynomial degree.
methodhelp.sedrate_to_age: Integrates positive sedimentation rates into a depth–age model with explicit interval rules and units.
methodhelp.series_summary: Descriptive statistics for sample count, location and dispersion; leaves the input unchanged.
methodhelp.welch_spectrum: Averages PSDs from complete segments, each detrended and tapered. X must be strictly increasing and uniform. Choose segment length before overlap in samples, which must be smaller than length. The default 256-sample segment is not automatically shortened. FFT 0 uses segment length. Incomplete tail segments are not padded; overlapping segments are not independent. Use an evolutionary spectrum to retain position-dependent estimates.

parameterhelp.evo_normalize: Off: retain PSD and compare absolute power across windows. On: divide each window by its full one-sided maximum power. The map and mean spectrum become relative power, useful for comparing cycle positions. Strong and weak windows can then have equally bright peaks, so color no longer compares absolute strength. parameterhelp.outlier_method: Hampel targets local spikes. Global MAD compares the whole record and may flag trends or different stratigraphic regimes. Bounds use the original Y unit.
parameterhelp.outlier_window: An odd window of at least 3 points. Edges use available neighbors. Used by Hampel detection and local-median replacement; short windows may flag genuine short-period signals.
parameterhelp.outlier_threshold: Multiplier of 1.4826 × MAD, default 3. With zero MAD, values differing from the median are flagged. Not used by bounds detection.
parameterhelp.outlier_lower: Values below this bound are flagged; equality is retained. Uses the Y unit.
parameterhelp.outlier_upper: Values above this bound are flagged; equality is retained. Uses the Y unit.
parameterhelp.outlier_action: Mark-only leaves values unchanged unless manually excluded. Exclusion removes X/Y points without filling gaps; replacement uses the original local input median. methodhelp.value_transform:
Compute ln(y/s), log10(y/s), asinh(y/s), or tanh(y/s), with positive scale s. X is unchanged and output is dimensionless. Logarithms require all Y > 0; no offset is added automatically. asinh accepts positive, negative, and zero values and compresses large magnitudes. tanh maps values to −1…1 and saturates at extremes.
These transformations change amplitude meaning and downstream statistics. They do not classify outliers or fill missing intervals. Record the function and scale and compare against the original record.
parameterhelp.value_transform: Logarithms require positive values. asinh handles signed values; tanh is bounded and saturates. Transformation is not outlier removal.
parameterhelp.transform_scale: Positive scale in the input Y unit. The function acts on y/s and returns a dimensionless value. Choose the scale for the research question; it is not estimated automatically.

parameterhelp.evo_window_mode: Define the window in samples or as a percentage of this node's input X span, after upstream processing. Longer windows separate nearby frequencies better but localize short changes less precisely. Include enough cycles for your question. The 20% preset is a starting point, not a universal optimum. New tasks and legacy workflows still default to sample counts.
parameterhelp.evo_window_percent: L=round((N−1)×percentage/100), using this node’s actual input N and rounding positive half-integers upward. At least 8 samples; no automatic enlargement. Under this rule 100% gives N−1 samples; use sample mode to include all N. Endpoint span is (L−1)×dx. Choose the periods of interest first; overlap cannot compensate for an overly short window.
parameterhelp.evo_step_mode: Samples: move by a fixed number of samples for exact reproduction. Overlap: derive the step from window length and overlap percentage. Target window count: derive an integer step from this node's actual input and window length so the complete-window count does not exceed the target; useful across inputs of different lengths. None changes the sampling interval or pads the boundaries. Saved workflows keep their mode until you change it or apply the preset.
parameterhelp.evo_overlap_percent: Used only in Overlap mode. Step S=max(1,round(L×(1−overlap/100))); actual overlap is 100×(1−S/L), recorded in the preview and report. For a 100-sample window, 99.2% requests a one-sample step, giving 99% in practice. Greater overlap samples window positions more densely but adds neither independent observations nor true frequency resolution. 99.2% is not a universal optimum.
parameterhelp.evo_fft_mode: Enter FFT samples directly or use a multiple of the window samples.
parameterhelp.evo_padding: FFT samples = window samples × multiplier. Zero padding each extracted window densifies the frequency grid without adding observations or improving true frequency resolution. This differs from padding both ends of the full series: this task uses complete windows only. Larger multipliers usually cost more memory and computation; budgets still apply.
parameter.evo_amplitude: Default map: square root of power
parameterhelp.evo_amplitude: Initially display square roots of nonnegative power with smooth rendering. After per-window normalization this is relative amplitude; otherwise it is square root of PSD, not signal amplitude. Database, CSV, probes and mean spectrum retain power. Switch the display in heatmap styles.

parameterhelp.evo_target_windows: Controls map sampling along time/depth, not the number of independent observations. A finer grid adds no observations.
parameterhelp.preprocess.spacing: Used only with fixed/specified spacing, in X units. For X in ka, 0.1 means 0.1 ka; editing a unit label does not convert values. Spacing must allow at least two grid points within the range and respect output-size and floating-point resolution limits.
parameterhelp.preprocess.interpolation: Linear joins adjacent observations. Natural cubic spline uses zero endpoint second derivatives; Akima constructs piecewise cubics from local slopes. They require at least 2, 3 and 5 distinct X values after cleanup, respectively. Insufficient samples cause an error, not an automatic method change. Used only when resampling; inspect peaks and long gaps rather than assuming a smoother curve is more accurate.
parameterhelp.sampling_check.gap_factor: Flags adjacent positive intervals strictly greater than median positive interval × factor; equality is not flagged. Default 3; increasing it reduces flags. Negative and zero intervals do not enter the median. Check ordering first for unordered input; the statistic is unavailable when there are no positive intervals.
parameterhelp.fft_spectrum.psd_nfft: 0 uses the full input length, not the next power of two. Explicit length must accommodate the entire input; maximum 262144. Additional points densify the frequency grid without extending observations or improving true resolution.
parameterhelp.welch_spectrum.psd_nfft: 0 uses each segment length, not full input length. Explicit length must accommodate a segment; maximum 262144. Padding applies within extracted segments, without completing the record tail or adding independent observations.
parameterhelp.welch_spectrum.psd_window: Samples per spectral estimate: at least 8 and no more than current input length. Longer segments generally improve separation but reduce the number averaged; shorter segments do the reverse. Only complete segments are used; the default 256 is not automatically shortened.
parameterhelp.welch_spectrum.psd_overlap: Shared samples between adjacent segments, not a percentage. Must be smaller than segment length. Step = segment length − overlap; default 128/256 means 50%. Recheck after changing length. More overlap does not add independent observations.
